title: Value embeddings on every layer (FLOP-free capacity)
description: has_ve() now returns True for all layers, so all 12 layers get a value embedding instead of the 6 odd ones; params 71.3M -> 96.5M at unchanged FLOPs/token. val_bpb 0.987376 vs baseline 0.986277 (worse by 0.0011).
reflection: Negative, and informative. The cheapness prediction held exactly: 25M extra params cost only 2.5% of the token budget (331.5M -> 323.1M tokens, MFU 38.5% -> 37.5%, VRAM 32.1 -> 33.0 GB) because value embeddings are excluded from the FLOP count and involve no matmul. The capacity prediction failed: despite paying almost nothing in tokens, val_bpb got worse by 0.0011, just past the ~0.0009 noise floor. That is a stronger result than a tie would have been. Round 4's reading was that we sit at the compute-optimal size and capacity trades 1:1 against tokens; this run shows capacity loses even when it is nearly free, so the model is no longer capacity-limited in any direction. Layer 0 having no VE, which I flagged as a likely gap, evidently was not one. Plausible mechanism for the small loss: the ve_gate is zero-initialised to a NEUTRAL 1.0 rather than off, so six new value-residual paths are live from step 0 and add variance to the residual stream; rescuing the idea would mean initialising the gate near off, which I do not think is worth a slot. Consolidated dead axes after 25 runs: batch size (flat), head split (-0.0028 wrong way), width 512->640 (flat), depth beyond 12 (projected at noise floor), FLOP-free capacity (this, negative). The untouched region is quality-per-token at fixed parameter count: WINDOW_PATTERN (SSSL is an unexamined speed hack), the LR schedule shape (WARMUP_RATIO 0.0, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5, never probed), and WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2.
